invariants_verified: Versioned atlas.mission-store/v1 local persistence envelope stores Missions, lifecycle events, steps, waits, Decisions, Actions, Receipts and receipt links.
Private atomic file writes plus a private operation lock preserve exact Mission state across process restart and serialize concurrent writers.
Mission lifecycle transitions reuse appendMissionLifecycleEvent and reject conflicting event IDs or idempotency keys while allowing exact replay.
Every repository read and write requires the server-derived tenant, organisation, project and environment scope; dependent records require an existing scoped Mission.
Governed Decisions, Actions and Receipts are contract-validated before persistence; committed Actions are checked against their matching Decision.
The PostgreSQL migration is additive and expand/contract-shaped, with tenant-keyed primary keys, idempotency uniqueness and foreign-key parent integrity.

verification.command: cd packages/atlas && npm run metadata:write && npm test && npm run build

limitations: The executable backend is a zero-credential private local file store only.
The PostgreSQL migration is a shipped contract artifact and was not executed against disposable PostgreSQL in this environment.
CI, staging, provider sandbox, limited production and production maturity remain unclaimed.
Outbox workers, leases, provider execution, billing settlement and hosted Cloud persistence remain later work.
verdict: ATLAS-BMR2-P1-004 = PASS — durable Mission persistence is locally proven with restart, replay, isolation, concurrency and migration contract coverage; PostgreSQL/CI/staging/production proof remains unclaimed.
